entities.name: Interscope Records
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Interscope Records, founded in 1990 by Jimmy Iovine and Ted Field as an independent label distributed by WEA (Warner), is one of the most commercially successful and artistically significant American record labels of the 1990s-2010s — achieving prominence through its relationship with Death Row Records (distributing Snoop Dogg, Tupac, and the birth of West Coast gangsta rap), its signing of Dr. Dre's Aftermath label, and its development of major artists including Nine Inch Nails, Eminem, Lady Gaga, Kendrick Lamar, and U2's later catalog.

Jimmy Iovine's trajectory from recording engineer (working with Springsteen, Patti Smith, John Lennon) to executive reflects Interscope's combination of technical recording knowledge and commercial instincts. The label's early signing of Suge Knight and Dr. Dre's Death Row relationship (1992-1996) distributed Snoop Dogg's Doggystyle, Tupac's All Eyez on Me, and Dre's The Chronic — albums that defined West Coast hip-hop and sold tens of millions worldwide. Despite controversy over Death Row's gangsta rap content (Congressional hearings, Tipper Gore's PMRC), Interscope maintained the relationship.

After Death Row's collapse following Tupac's murder (1996) and Suge Knight's imprisonment, Interscope acquired Dr. Dre's Aftermath Entertainment and signed Eminem (through Aftermath) — creating one of the most commercially successful label-within-label relationships in hip-hop history. Lady Gaga's career was developed entirely through Interscope. Today Interscope (now part of Universal Music Group's Interscope Geffen A&M division) remains one of American popular music's most powerful label imprints.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Interscope Records — distributing West Coast gangsta rap's defining albums, developing Eminem and Lady Gaga, and navigating music industry controversies from PMRC to streaming — is one of the most commercially successful and artistically consequential American labels of the past 30 years.
